subject: Latency & stability experimentation worksheet — Octavia RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@octavia-fin.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Octavia Procurement <procurement@octavia-fin.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFP: performance profile and experiment details

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick intro call last week. As part of our RFP for inference providers we need a concise, experiment-oriented set of artifacts focused on latency stability and throughput scaling. Specifically, procurement has asked for:

- A compact test plan we can run in our environment (or follow as-is) that exercises concurrent short-chat requests and longer-document generations.
- A table of expected p50/p95/p99 for short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=1024 tokens) sequences at several concurrency points.
- A short script or harness we can run (or extend) so results are comparable.

Can you provide the above by EOD Friday? We want to include a snapshot in the scoring matrix.

Best,
Sanjay Reddy
Head of Platform Engineering
Octavia Financial
From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@octavia-fin.com>, procurement@octavia-fin.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-18T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP: performance profile and experiment details

Sanjay —

Thanks for the scope. We can absolutely deliver an experimentation worksheet and a runnable harness. Quick clarifications so we tailor the artifacts:

1) Traffic mix: do you want a separate short-chat workload and a long-generation workload, or a blended mix that approximates your production 70:30 short:long?
2) Network topology: will you run tests from a single VM in your VPC (recommended) or from distributed agents across regions?
3) Success criteria: do you score based on p95 only, or p99 and error-rate thresholds as well?

I've attached a compact spreadsheet we usually share for procurement-level scoring and a small test script that runs against a Redwood-dedicated endpoint (can be parameterized for your on-prem setup). Dev (cc'd) can help with any endpoint access or script tuning.

Deliverables:
- 20270522_performance_matrix.xlsx (attached): population of test points and expected metrics derived from our internal lab for the model family you evaluated.
- latency_test_script.sh (attached): lightweight harness (curl + concurrency wrapper) to reproduce short and long sequences.
- Execution notes in body and a short log sample (redwood-exec-log-05022.txt).

We will also include recommended guardrails (max concurrency, batching hints, cache warm-up steps) so your scoring team can get consistent outputs.

I can run through the sheet with your team on Thursday if helpful.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@octavia-fin.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-20T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP: performance profile and experiment details

Sanjay — quick notes about the harness and interpretation of the spreadsheet: 

- The attached script is intentionally minimal: it POSTs a request payload and measures end-to-end wall time. It supports a small concurrency driver (xargs + parallel) so you can sweep qps.
- For short requests we recommend payloads with <=64 output tokens and a fixed prompt length; for long-run tests we include a parameter to request 1200 token outputs.
- Warm-up: run 3x1min warm-up at target concurrency before taking samples to populate p50/p95/p99.
- Statistical confidence: our sheet documents sample counts we recommend (n>=1200 per test point) to stabilize p99. If you cannot run that many, note p99 will be noisy and you should prefer p95 for scoring.
- Batch and KV-cache influence: when you run the harness against your private deployment, disable any prefix caching for the long-run test to simulate cold prefixes, and enable typical caching for the short-chat test. We included a column in the sheet describing "cache on/off" scenarios.

If you want, Marissa can run a baseline in our dedicated cluster and share raw CSVs so you can compare line-by-line.

- Dev
Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Reddy <sanjay.reddy@octavia-fin.com>, procurement@octavia-fin.com
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-22T17:45:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP: performance profile and experiment details

Sanjay — following up with the baseline CSVs and a short readme. We spun the tests against a dedicated L4 pod (A100 equivalent) to generate the expected values in the spreadsheet. Highlighted observations:

- Short-chat workload (<=64 tokens): p50=12ms, p95=34ms, p99=78ms at concurrency 64 with batching disabled; with batching enabled p95 drops to 28ms and cost per token falls by ~18%.
- Long-generation workload (>=1024 tokens): p50=420ms, p95=1.1s, p99=1.9s at concurrency 4 (higher concurrencies induce queuing/backpressure on the model pipeline).
- Degradation modes: when CPU/IO contention rises on the control plane we observed tail spikes — recommended mitigation is to cap request concurrency per endpoint and enable our graceful-fallback policy to a quantized variant.

Attached: baseline-csvs.zip (referenced in Drive link), and the sheet/shell script from Ava's earlier message. We recommend the scoring team run three runs separated by 30 minutes and use the median p95 across runs.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the sheet and the CSVs tomorrow 10–10:30am PT if that works for your team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
